payload.name: Require actual existing memory before duplicate SKIP
payload.description: During construction CRUD decisions, when a candidate is marked SKIP as duplicate but the related-memory pool is empty or has no overlapping memory, apply this rule before dropping it.
content: Do not SKIP a candidate as duplicate unless the retrieved memory pool or current snapshot contains an actual existing memory with substantive overlap.
If related memories are empty or none overlaps the candidate, treat the candidate as new and ADD it; absence of a retrieved memory is not evidence of duplication.
When duplication is uncertain, prefer persisting the evidence-supported candidate rather than discarding it, because an unpersisted fact cannot be recovered later.

candidates.solves: Construction CRUD decisions sometimes SKIP an evidence-supported candidate as duplicate even though no existing memory was retrieved, so the fact is never persisted. This rule applies when a duplicate SKIP is considered and the related-memory pool is empty or contains no overlapping memory; it does not apply when a real overlapping memory exists, because then the SKIP is legitimate.

payload.name: Verify-before-skip-duplicate-in-construction
payload.description: When a construction decision is about to SKIP a candidate because its information is already included in an existing or updated memory, first verify that the referenced memory actually exists in the snapshot or accepted changes; if none exists, ADD or MERGE instead.
content: Before applying SKIP with a duplication reason (e.g., 'already included', 'already in memory'), locate the claimed existing memory in the current snapshot or in the batch of accepted ADD/UPDATE/MERGE operations for the session.

If no such memory exists, do not skip; treat the candidate as a new fact and ADD it (or MERGE if it partially overlaps). Rationales like 'Information already included in the updated memory' are only valid when a real memory with substantive overlap is visible.

candidates.solves: The construction agent dropped a valid extracted fact by SKIPping it with a duplication rationale even though no prior memory existed. This candidate arises when extracting facts from a conversation; future inputs with similar claims of duplication need a check that the referenced memory is real before discarding. The rule applies to any construction decision where a SKIP is based only on alleged existing coverage.

payload.name: ADD new facts when no merge target exists
payload.description: When a candidate describes a new fact, event, or state and no existing memory is relevant or retrieved, use ADD instead of SKIP.
content: If a candidate represents new information (a fact, event, or state) and no existing memory is found to update or merge with, the absence of a merge target is the trigger for ADD, not SKIP.
Before skipping, confirm whether the candidate is genuinely new knowledge; if so, persist it as a new memory even when no related memory exists.

candidates.solves: During construction CRUD, the agent sometimes SKIPs a candidate for a new fact/event/state with the reason 'No relevant memory to update or merge with.' This misinterprets the role of the existing-memory pool: a missing merge target is the normal precondition for creating a new memory, not a reason to discard the candidate. This rule applies to any future session where an extracted candidate contains previously unseen information and no related memory is found.

payload.name: Verify existing memory before SKIP as already included
payload.description: When a construction candidate is marked SKIP because the information is already included, use this before deciding.
content: During the decision stage, before choosing SKIP with the reason 'information already included', verify that the candidate's core fact is actually present in a retrieved existing memory or in an already-accepted update from the same batch; if no such memory exists, do not skip. Instead, ADD the candidate (or UPDATE an existing related memory) so the fact is persisted.
Only use SKIP when the exact core information is already durably stored and no update/merge is needed; a stale, imagined, or batch-internal reason does not justify discarding the candidate.

candidates.solves: During construction decision, a candidate may be skipped with the rationale that its information is already included even though no current memory contains it, permanently losing a user-stated fact. This rule applies whenever the CRUD stage evaluates ADD/UPDATE vs SKIP against the memory pool and must verify actual existence before skipping; it does not apply to extraction or to cases where an existing memory genuinely covers the candidate.

payload.name: Verify duplicate-skip against actual memory state
payload.description: When a construction candidate is about to be SKIPped as 'already included', first verify that a current or successfully applied memory actually contains that fact; otherwise ADD the candidate.
content: During CRUD decisions, only SKIP a candidate when a matching memory exists in the current snapshot or in changes already applied in this batch; a reason like 'already included' is not sufficient without that evidence.
If no existing or successfully applied memory contains the candidate's fact, ADD it, even when a sibling candidate from the same message is also being skipped.

candidates.solves: Future construction batches may SKIP a candidate for being 'already included' although no current or newly applied memory contains that fact, losing information. This rule applies when a duplicate-skip lacks concrete evidence; it does not apply when a matching memory version actually exists, where SKIP remains correct.

payload.name: Duplicate-skip requires existing memory match
payload.description: Use during construction CRUD when a candidate is being skipped as a duplicate. Verify that a retrieved existing memory actually contains the same fact before skipping; otherwise add the candidate.
content: When considering SKIP for a candidate because it seems duplicate, first check the retrieved existing memories. Only SKIP if an existing memory clearly contains the same fact about the same subject with equivalent detail. Otherwise, ADD the candidate.

Do not infer duplication from general knowledge, prior turns, or earlier commits unless a retrieved memory still exists in the current session pool. If the pool is empty or unrelated, the candidate is not redundant.

candidates.solves: Construction agents sometimes SKIP a valid extraction candidate by claiming it duplicates an existing memory even when no such memory is present in the retrieved pool, causing the fact to be lost. This rule requires that a duplicate-based SKIP be grounded in a visible matching memory; when the pool lacks the fact, the candidate must be added. Applies to any construction decision where SKIP is chosen for duplication.

payload.name: No duplicate skip on empty related pool
payload.description: Apply during construction CRUD when a candidate is about to be SKIPped as duplicate or redundant: verify the retrieved related-memory pool is non-empty and contains a memory semantically covering the candidate; if not, ADD it instead.
content: During the decision stage, before applying SKIP with a duplicate/redundant reason, confirm that the retrieved related-memory pool is non-empty and contains an existing memory that actually covers the candidate's information. If the pool is empty or no related memory overlaps, do not SKIP; perform ADD.

candidates.solves: Construction candidates were incorrectly SKIPped as duplicates even though the retrieved related-memory pool was empty, so evidence-backed facts were never persisted. This rule grounds any duplicate/redundant skip in an actual retrieved related memory and applies to future CRUD decisions where a candidate would be skipped without supporting related memory.

payload.name: Verify-Existing-Before-Skip
payload.description: Apply before SKIPping a construction candidate as already represented: confirm a matching memory is actually present in the retrieved memory pool; if absent, ADD the candidate.
content: Before choosing SKIP with the reason that a candidate is already represented, require a concrete matching memory from the retrieved existing-memory pool.
If the retrieved pool contains no memory matching the candidate's subject and key content, the candidate is new information and must be ADDed, not skipped.

candidates.solves: Construction agents sometimes skip adding a valid new memory because they assume an equivalent memory already exists, even when the retrieved memory pool contains no such memory. This causes facts to be lost. The skill forces the agent to ground any duplication-based SKIP in an actual memory from the retrieved pool, and to ADD otherwise. It applies to any future session where extracted candidates are evaluated for ADD vs SKIP.

operations.name: Verify Existing Memory Before Duplicate SKIP
operations.description: Use when a construction CRUD decision is about to SKIP a candidate as duplicate or already included.
content: Before applying SKIP with a duplication reason, confirm that a matching memory actually exists in the current snapshot or in changes already applied in this batch.
If no such memory exists, do not skip; ADD the candidate (or MERGE if it partially overlaps).
An empty or unrelated retrieved memory pool is not evidence of duplication; absence of a merge target is the normal precondition for ADD.
